findings.conclusion: NtCreateFile uses OBJ_DONT_REPARSE plus FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT, creation-only protected current-user security, and excludes FILE_SHARE_DELETE. The exact returned handle is validated before return.

Child open/exists/replacement use the retained handle final_path to reconstruct absolute paths rather than NtCreateFile RootDirectory relative handle operations. Final string comparison alone is not a general object-identity proof. Correctness depends on the retained root and relevant ancestry remaining namespace-pinned for the supported filesystem/host.

The read test asserts both root and ancestor rename fail while directory is retained, completes write/sync/MoveFileEx/re-read during retention, then asserts both renames succeed after handles drop. Acquisition substitution test constructs real private ACL leaves and performs the real rename+junction in a pre-open hook; rejection cannot be satisfied merely by ACL mismatch.

The owner independently reports the exact prior-host retained-directory test passed, and is preparing fresh combined-head native qualification. This review does not independently execute or replace that qualification, nor infer universal filesystem semantics.

Creation descriptor storage outlives synchronous creation, owner is explicitly current process user, and existing descriptor is not silently repaired. ACL in-use span, complete SID, handle kind and single-link checks are present. No newly confirmed scope-relevant defect found in this bounded static review.

boundaries: No proof for arbitrary SMB/custom filesystem behavior
Not isolation from the same user SID, trusted administrators or LocalSystem
No broad statement about unrelated Windows adaptation layers
Prior selector-native qualification is not a fresh all-owner-suite pass
